_comment: Wall-clock seconds for one bats file in its own bats call on a GitHub windows-latest runner, Node 20. Used ONLY to balance CI shards -- never to gate anything. Stale numbers cost balance, never correctness: shard-tests.mjs asserts every file lands in exactly one shard whether or not it appears here.
_why: arc-ci's windows leg costs 1585s against ~145s on ubuntu for the same 563 tests -- 2.82s per test against 0.26s, because every bats `run` spawns a process and windows process creation is dear. Measured 2026-07-31 (run 30611012771): excluding the workspace and bats' binaries from Microsoft Defender changes nothing, because the runner image already ships with realtime protection OFF and both drives excluded. There is no windows-side saving left to find, so the fix stays splitting.
_provenance: 112 of 115 discovered files re-measured in a single pass on 2026-08-12 (run 31627029442, weigh-tests.yml, on feat/arc-bench-slice-06) -- one file per job on windows-latest, each timed in its own bats call with the scanners arc-ci installs, the same method as every earlier pass. Re-run that workflow and paste its block rather than editing numbers by hand. The previous pass (2026-08-10, run 31361908896) measured 104 files; this one closes the gap for the bench files, whose absence had been riding _default_weight and skewing the shard plan.
_evidence: The 2026-08-10 pass measured 104 files, 44 of which had NO entry at all and were riding _default_weight 16. The two this slice grew were among them and wrong in the same direction by roughly sevenfold: leads-journey.bats 111s and leads-mail-guard.bats 120s. (An earlier version of this sentence said 47 covered; 47 was the count MISSING before the run, 44 of them were measured, and the other 3 are the ones _known_gap names.) The method is unchanged from the pass that produced the previous table: one file per job on windows, each timed in its own bats call with the scanners arc-ci installs.
_floor: spine-emit.bats at 160s is the floor no shard count can beat, and design-steel-thread.bats at 156s is second. Both numbers are from the 2026-08-10 pass; the previous prose here quoted 147s and 128s from the 2026-08-03 pass and was left standing when the table under it was replaced -- a measured claim that stops being re-derived starts lying, which is the whole reason this file records provenance. From 12 shards on, the heaviest shard IS that one file, and one file cannot be split.
_known_gap: 3 file(s) measured RED in isolation on windows and are therefore NOT re-weighted from this pass: arc-profile.bats, arc-scan.bats, baseline.bats. Their elapsed time is the time they took to FAIL, which is not the time they take to run. Previous weights retained: arc-profile.bats (kept 39s), arc-scan.bats (kept 58s), baseline.bats (kept 42s). THE RED IS NOT A BENCH REGRESSION AND NOT NEW: the identical three files fail identically in isolation on main (run 31625002487, same day, same method) -- arc-profile 36s, arc-scan 55s, baseline 20s, all rc=1. They PASS in arc-ci only when sharded alongside arc-tools-image.bats, which prepares the arc-tools docker image the semgrep adapter falls back to. That is an UNDECLARED INTER-FILE DEPENDENCY: they pass by shard luck, and any change to the shard plan revokes it. This field exists because an unmeasured entry is a DEFAULT rather than an error (retro-log 2026-08-03); name a new file here rather than letting it disappear. PLUS 4 file(s) added on 2026-08-13 that this pass PREDATES and therefore never measured: bench-core.bats, bench-drift.bats, bench-proposal.bats, bench-seal.bats. They are riding _default_weight 16 and every one of them is far heavier than that -- each runs a probe that spawns full K=3 bench runs, so the plan is under-weighting them by roughly an order of magnitude. NO ESTIMATE IS WRITTEN HERE: a number nobody measured, in a table of measurements, is the thing this file exists to prevent. The fix is a weigh-tests run against a tree that contains them; this note is the COUNT that keeps the gap from disappearing into the default in the meantime (M10).
